text: n is meant to have a single prime factor, as 'the prime factor' (R-RET-4) presupposes, i.e. n is a prime power such as 4, 8 or 9; a call whose n has several distinct prime factors is outside the contract (contradicts reading 1, which the words 'not a prime' alone allow)
on n <= 1 or prime n the call must still return an integer normally; only the returned value is unconstrained
any number numerically equal to the required prime factor (for example the float 3.0) is acceptable
any prime factor of n is acceptable (the definite article is loose)
